summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic published Tom Allen's recollections of his 23 battles from 1860 to 1879, including his 1869 fight with Charley Gallagher on Chouteau Island, where a ringside shot struck his right hand.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Sunday Morning, March 31, 1895, page 40.

facts.fact: Allen fought Posh Price in England in 1862 as a lightweight and was beaten in 35 rounds
Three years after his first fight with Posh Price, Allen, then a middleweight at 146 pounds, beat him in 41 rounds
Allen fought 23 battles between 1860 and 1879, six of them between January 12, 1869 and November 5, 1870; McCool forfeited $1,000 on a further match
Allen fought Bill Davis on January 12, 1869
Allen lost to Charley Gallagher in the second round when he stepped into a snow-filled hole in the ring, slipped, and was struck on the neck
Allen's fight with Mike McCool on June 15, 1869 at Foster's Island was declared a draw when the McCool party broke into the ring in the tenth round

Allen beat Charley Gallagher in the eleventh round on August 17, 1869 at Chouteau Island before about 1,400 spectators, after a shot from the ringside struck his right hand; Dr. Nidelet removed the bullet and the fight resumed
Allen said he knew who fired the shot at the Gallagher fight and that it was meant for him
Allen said he trained down from 231 to 160 pounds for his fight with McCool
facts.quote: Talk about coming down to the bottom—in my fight with McCool I went from 231 to 160.

facts.fact: In England Allen fought Baltimore Bob Smith barefoot, the day after the match was made, and was beaten in fifty minutes; Smith had twice beaten Allen's brother Harry
